clue.text: Diminished in role as editor

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: found across the end of role, all of as and the start of editor

explanation.surface: An editor has been demoted, given a lesser part to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain or pressure that has eased has lessened, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: The definition here is not put into words!

definitions.text: The definition here is not put into words!

parts.words: The definition here is not put into words!
parts.note: surface reading: a puzzling remark that this clue has no wording for its definition
setter's reading: the definition is the closing punctuation symbol itself, which is a mark rather than a word

explanation.surface: The clue seems to confess that it forgot to include a definition at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends with its own definition: the final symbol is the thing named, and a symbol is indeed not put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing '!' is the punctuation symbol of surprise, the very thing the answer names.

clue.text: Cinema technique showing Frenchman entering second smallest room

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second

indicators.note: something entering a room goes inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: the smallest room is a jocular name for the lavatory
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A film shows a Frenchman walking into the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Second gives S, which stands outside the container; only the loo takes in the Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow motion, abbreviated, is a filming effect where action is shown slower than real speed.

clue.text: Frustrate a proposed law over European lack of attention

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin or frustrate them
a bill is a law not yet passed
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A government blocks a bill because of Europe's indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first pieces sit above the European. Dishabille is a state of being carelessly or partly dressed, so the definition means lack of attention to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishabille is a careless, half-dressed state, showing neglect of one's appearance.

clue.text: Eccentric person not natural, perhaps, as cheat

parts.note: a card is an amusingly odd character
in music a note that is not natural may be sharp; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: An odd, artificial person is exposed as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not natural' reads as artificial, but it is the musical sense: a sharp note is raised from the natural one.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-sharp is a swindler who wins at cards by trickery.

clue.text: Reptile, angry, spitting out article worked in wool

parts.note: short for crocodile

indicators.note: spitting something out expels it, so a word loses the item named

parts.note: a heated person is angry
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A furious crocodile spits out a knitted item.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATED drops its A to leave HETED, giving CROC + HETED.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocheted describes something made with a hooked needle from yarn such as wool.

clue.text: Cavalryman to free soldiers up

parts.note: to rid is to free of something

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the usual crossword soldiers

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier sets about freeing his comrades.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman is a soldier on horseback, so a horse rider.

clue.text: No hardliners turning up for a difficult situation

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue flips the word to read from the bottom upward

parts.note: in British politics, wets were moderate Conservatives who opposed Thatcher's hard line

explanation.surface: When moderates fail to show, trouble follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' was the 1980s label for moderate Tories, the opposite of hardliners.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being in an agitated, awkward predicament.

clue.text: Accomplishing anti-anti-G, possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written, hyphens ignored

explanation.surface: It reads like a quirky label for defeating gravity, as in a space feat.
explanation.definitionFit: Attaining a goal means achieving or bringing it about, a synonym of accomplishing.

clue.text: Resonant paragon? That's quite wrong

indicators.note: something entirely wrong is completely out of order, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that calling a person a shining model is quite mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: far from a celebrated paragon, this person is unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is Latin for an unwelcome person, the reverse of a celebrated model of virtue.

clue.text: Angry news hound is contributor to newspaper

parts.note: cross means annoyed
word in the sense of news, as in 'any word?'
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A furious newshound writes for a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News hound' looks like a journalist, but it splits into two separate pieces. The answer is the self-referential job of the person who wrote this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers print puzzles compiled by setters, so the setter supplies part of each day's newspaper.

clue.text: Garment tailor has altered to accommodate height

indicators.note: to accommodate is to make room for a guest, so one more letter is taken in
altered means changed, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A tailor has let out a garment to make room for a taller wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: The height letter joins the fodder before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An aloha shirt is a brightly patterned Hawaiian shirt, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Big vehicle? Millions in fuel, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front
'in' places one item inside the other

parts.note: oil is a fuel
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A large car, someone muses, burns millions in petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes after the O of OIL, and the result is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxury car; the question mark flags that size is only one of its traits.

clue.text: Faint winds waft, offering no initial protection against cold weather

indicators.note: something that winds twists about, so the word before it is twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with no initial, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a waft is a gentle breeze

explanation.surface: Light winds blow, giving no early shelter from the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faint winds' reads as gentle breezes, but winds is a verb acting on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is added to car engines to stop the coolant freezing in winter.

clue.text: Not believing robbery left incomplete in high-level area

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened word inside the other

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house

indicators.note: left incomplete means the word is cut short, losing its end

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A sceptic's account of an unfinished burglary in a top-floor room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' tempts as the usual L, but here 'left incomplete' just says the robbery word is cut short by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheistic means rejecting belief in any god, so not believing.

clue.text: Joint, food, party — male's laid-back state?

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
a pie is a type of food
a do is a party
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A spliff, snacks and a party: that is a man's relaxed life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a cannabis cigarette, which fits the hippie picture, but here it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippiedom is the relaxed, counter-cultural world of hippies, a famously easy-going lifestyle.

clue.text: Company to start operating a railway as a result

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
cameras or machines roll when they start running
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A firm begins running a train line as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A corollary is a consequence or natural result that follows from something else.

clue.text: African dismissing farthing and cent, backing African currency

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
dismissing sends things away, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written: the first of the two Africans in the clue
F is the abbreviation for farthing, an old British quarter-penny coin
C is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: An African rejects old coins in favour of a local currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F and C from AFRICAN leaves ARIAN, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the monetary unit of Nigeria.

clue.text: Force politician into middle of field

indicators.note: 'into' places one piece inside another
the middle of a word is its centre letters, without the ends

parts.note: the central letters of field
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone forces a politician onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone into action, as force does as a verb.

clue.text: Mistaken to block return of unusual bravery

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in its path, so one piece goes inside the other
a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: odd means unusual
erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: A mistaken move blocks the comeback of something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion lands after the first letter of the reversed word, so the result begins and ends with D.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is an old-fashioned word for daring, heroic action.

clue.text: Apprehend American's in love

indicators.note: 'is in' places one letter inside the following word

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, so nil
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American has fallen in love.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', putting the American letter inside NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a criminal is an informal idiom for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Heavens — poet's good for frolicking

parts.note: the heavens are the sky
Philip Larkin was an English poet
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a poet's work is fit for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens' looks like an exclamation of surprise but supplies the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarking is horseplay or playing about, so it means the same as frolicking.

clue.text: Take a lower position, note, aboard boat

indicators.note: being aboard means being inside a vessel, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, chiefly on the Tyne
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Someone is told to crouch down, with a memo, on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling means lowering the body onto the knees, getting into a lower posture.

clue.text: Divine to give up a little time for Northern people

indicators.note: giving something up means letting it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to divine is to sense by intuition
T is the abbreviation for time, little because it is a single letter

explanation.surface: A god sacrifices a moment for the sake of Arctic folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective or a god, but it is the verb meaning to guess; INTUIT loses one T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous peoples of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.

clue.text: Exclusive work at last?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: only, belonging to one alone
second meaning: the underside of a shoe, which a cobbler works on a last, the foot-shaped block

explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally', but a last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped mould; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means one and only, and also the bottom of a shoe that a shoemaker fits on the mould.

clue.text: Heavenly sight misinterpreted as adorable and mundane?

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so the letters are taken in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beautiful view in the sky is mistakenly called both lovely and dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' between the two words only joins them; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andromeda nebula, now known as a galaxy, is visible in the night sky.

clue.text: Milky beer distributed in part of Australia

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cloudy beer is being sold across a region of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kimberley is a large region in the north of Western Australia.

clue.text: Further times and further time included in time

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sports report: more matches, then extra time inside the allotted time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And further' here only means 'plus'; the times sign and time letter go inside ERA after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, beyond what is usual, the same as further as an adjective.
